options.systemPromptTemplate: You classify inbound enquiries for a commercial rooftop solar installer. intent must be one of: quote_request, site_assessment, financing_enquiry, general_enquiry, maintenance_existing, supplier_pitch, job_application, spam. urgency must be one of: high, medium, low. budgetSignal must be one of: stated, implied, none. propertyType, roofType and siteOwnership should be extracted ONLY if the sender actually states them - never infer them. monthlyKwh is the stated monthly electricity consumption in kWh, 0 if not mentioned. painPoint is a short phrase in the sender's own terms. confidence is 0 to 1 reflecting how clearly the message states its purpose. A message that says nothing specific is general_enquiry with low confidence - never guess.

messageValues.message: You write brief, concrete replies for a commercial rooftop solar installer. You never quote prices, savings, payback periods, system sizes, tariffs, grants or tax credits - every one of those depends on a site assessment and stating one prematurely is a commercial and regulatory risk. You mirror the sender's own description of their problem rather than restating it in marketing language.

parameters.content:
## Setup needed

**Airtable** - base is already connected. Create two tables:

**Leads** - email (unique), name, company, phone, source, message, intent, urgency, score, tier, consent, accountStatus, assignedRep, assignedRepEmail, status, assignedAt, ackDueAt, escalatedAt, previousRep

**Important - accountStatus:** set it to "customer" for real customers. Scoring looks at THIS field, not just whether the email is already in the table - otherwise anyone who enquired twice would be treated as a customer.

**Sales Reps** - repName, repEmail (unique), slackUserId, tier, active, lastAssignedAt

Add at least one rep for each tier: enterprise (large business), smb (small business), existing_customer - plus one with tier "manager" for escalations. slackUserId is used to @mention the rep. lastAssignedAt updates after each assignment so leads rotate fairly between reps.

**Google Sheets** - a file named "Lead Automation" with tabs: Lead Log, Escalation Log, Error Log. Connect a Google Sheets credential (Drive or Calendar logins won't work).

**Website form secret** - the webhook only accepts requests that carry a secret header. Create a Header Auth credential (e.g. name `X-Voltara-Key`, value = a long random string), select it in **New Lead From Website Form**, and have the website's server send the same header. Keep the secret server-side, never in browser JavaScript.

**Errors** - already wired: Settings > Error Workflow points at this workflow. Re-select it if you import a copy.

## Why the form gets a reply first

The visitor gets a "received" reply right after their name and email are checked - in under a second. The AI reading, scoring and reply-writing all happen after that.

If the form waited for the AI to finish, it could time out and show the visitor an error - even though their details were saved.

Good to know: steps after the reply must pull lead details from **Clean Up Form Data** by name, because the reply step replaces the data being passed along.

## Rules set the score - AI only reads the message

The AI never decides the score. It only reads the message (what they want, how urgent, any budget hints). A fixed set of rules then adds or removes points.

This keeps scores easy to explain - each lead lists exactly why it got its score - and changing the rules doesn't mean rewriting AI prompts.

**Lead type is decided in this order:**
1. Duplicate - already an open lead from this email in the last 24 hours. Logged only: no second email, no second Slack alert.
2. Low priority - support requests, job applications or spam. This comes before customer status, so a customer asking for support isn't treated as a sales lead.
3. Existing customer - accountStatus is "customer".
4. Large business (65+ points) / Small business (35+) / otherwise Low priority.

parameters.content:
## 1 · Receive the lead & reply fast

The website form sends the lead here. Name and email are checked, and the visitor gets a "received" reply in under a second. Everything else happens after.

If the form waited for the AI, it could time out and show the visitor an error even though their details were saved.

**Note:** later steps pull lead details from **Clean Up Form Data** by name, because the reply step replaces the data being passed along.

## 2 · Check if we know them

Looks up the email in the Leads table. The scoring step uses this to spot existing customers (**accountStatus = customer**) and repeat leads from the last 24 hours.

It checks accountStatus, not just whether the email exists - every lead is saved to this table, so that would mark anyone who enquired before as a customer.

## 3 · AI reads the message

The AI reads the message for: what they want, how urgent it is, budget hints, and any solar details they mention (building type, roof type, own or rent, electricity use). It's told never to guess these - a made-up roof type would throw off the score.

## 4 · Score & sort - by rules, not AI

The AI never sets the score. It reads the message; this step adds up points using fixed rules.

**Biggest factors:**
- Monthly electricity use (up to +30) - the strongest sign of a good fit
- Owns the building (+20) - renters need landlord approval
- Flat or metal roof (+14 / +12) - easiest to install on
- Asbestos roof (-25) - must be dealt with first
- Roof 20+ years old (-15) - likely needs replacing first
- Home, not a business (-40) - we only do commercial

Every lead lists the reasons behind its score.

## 5 · Assign a rep & save

Picks the rep for that lead type who was assigned least recently, so leads rotate fairly. Saves the lead with a 15-minute follow-up deadline, counted in business hours (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00) - an overnight lead is due at 08:15 next business morning. Then updates the rep's last-assigned time.

If Airtable rejects the save, the team gets a Slack alert with the full lead so nobody is lost.

The rep update runs on a side branch so it doesn't overwrite the lead details passed to the next steps.

## 6 · Reply & alert the rep

AI writes a short reply based on what the lead actually said. It's not allowed to mention prices, savings, payback time, system size, rates or grants - those all need a site visit first, and promising one early is risky.

If the AI fails, a safe standard reply is sent instead.

The Slack alert tells the rep their follow-up deadline (15 minutes, counted in business hours).

## 7 · Low-priority leads & logging

Low-priority and duplicate leads are saved here - no email, no rep alert.

Every lead is written to the Lead Log, including invalid form submissions, so you can tell a quiet week apart from a broken form.

## 8 · Follow-up check - runs every 5 minutes

This stops good leads slipping through the cracks. A lead nobody calls back is lost money.

Finds leads that have no rep, or weren't followed up by their deadline (15 business minutes), and reassigns them to the sales manager - noting which case it was.

**If there are no overdue leads, it simply stops** - nothing to do.

Everything is tracked in Airtable, so restarting n8n doesn't lose anything.

## 9 · If something breaks

This branch runs whenever a live run fails. It works because the workflow is its own error workflow (**Settings > Error Workflow = this workflow**). If you import or duplicate it, select the copy there again. Manual test runs don't trigger it.

The alert reminds you that if the failure happened after the form was submitted, the visitor already saw a "received" message - so look for a lead without a rep rather than assuming nothing was saved.
